data.label: Receive CSV File
data.description: Trigger when a new incoming CSV file is received for validation.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger based on file arrival. No ML, NLP, or LLM capability is required. It is pure workflow orchestration and therefore L0.

data.label: Load Validation Schema
data.description: Retrieve the expected column list, data types, required fields, and numeric range rules.
data.rationale: Loading validation rules from a predefined source is deterministic lookup behavior. L0 is sufficient because this step does not involve uncertainty, language understanding, or learned prediction.

data.label: Parse CSV Content
data.description: Read and structure the incoming CSV file into rows and columns for validation.
data.rationale: CSV parsing is deterministic file processing with known delimiters and schema structure. This is classic rule-based data extraction and requires no AI.

data.label: Check Expected Columns
data.description: Compare CSV headers against the expected schema and identify missing or unexpected columns.
data.rationale: This is a direct schema comparison using exact matching and set operations. It is fully deterministic and fits L0 with no need for ML or language reasoning.

data.label: Validate Data Types
data.description: Verify that each column value matches the data type defined in the schema.
data.rationale: Data type validation is a deterministic rules/regex/parsing task. Since the schema defines the expected types, this can be handled entirely with L0 logic.

data.label: Check Required Nulls
data.description: Flag null, empty, or missing values in fields marked as required.
data.rationale: Required-field null checking is simple deterministic validation. No uncertainty or model inference is needed, so L0 is the correct level.

data.label: Validate Numeric Ranges
data.description: Check numeric fields against acceptable minimum and maximum values from the schema.
data.rationale: Numeric range checks are pure rule-based comparisons against thresholds from the schema. This is fully deterministic L0 automation.

data.label: Aggregate Validation Errors
data.description: Collect all validation failures from column, type, null, and range checks into a single error set.
data.rationale: Aggregating validation results is deterministic data collection and concatenation. It does not require learning or language generation, so L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Generate Validation Report
data.description: Create a validation report listing all discovered errors and the overall file status.
data.rationale: Although this step produces a report, the output is a template-driven compilation of known validation results rather than open-ended language generation. It remains deterministic formatting and therefore L0.

data.label: Publish Validation Result
data.description: Output the completed validation report for downstream review or processing.
data.rationale: Publishing the final report is a deterministic workflow end action. It simply passes the produced artifact downstream, requiring no AI or probabilistic reasoning.

data.condition: required columns present or column issues recorded
data.label: if columns acceptable

message: This workflow is fully deterministic and fits entirely within L0 automation. It performs file ingestion, schema lookup, CSV parsing, rule-based validation checks, error aggregation, and report generation without any ML, NLP, LLM, tool-augmented reasoning, or multi-agent coordination.
